title: Programmes to Support Companies to Adopt More Age-friendly Work Practices
what_it_is: Programmes to Support Companies to Adopt More Age-friendly Work Practices

sections.label: WorkPro Job Redesign Grant
sections.summary: Over 1,800 companies employing about 20,000 older workers benefited from the WorkPro Job Redesign Grant since 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Since the WorkPro Job Redesign Grant started six years ago in 2013, over 1,800 companies employing about 20,000 older workers have benefited from the grant and redesigned their jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: In 2018, about 12,000 companies, employing about 92% of the 331,000 local employees aged 50 and above, reported that they have done so.

sections.label: Training rates and job redesign
sections.summary: Training rates for workers aged 50 to 64 rose from 26% in 2015 to 40% in 2018, and the Government supports organisation-wide job redesign.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The rate of training older workers aged between 50 and 64 has been rising steadily in recent years, from 26% in 2015 to 40% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Today, job redesign is mostly very task-specific and benefits only a few workers at a time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Hence, the Government supports the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers' recommendation which encourages employers to move beyond this, so that they can implement job redesign throughout their organisations and at the systems level.

sections.label: Employers advising older workers
sections.summary: The Government supports the Workgroup's recommendation to encourage employers to engage mature and older workers in structured career planning sessions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: As employers are more aware of the changes in industry and also demand and technology, they are well-placed to advise older workers on the type of training they need to stay relevant for the future economy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Hence, the Government also supports the Workgroup's recommendation to encourage employers to engage mature and older workers in structured career planning sessions.

sections.label: Re-employment of older workers
sections.summary: Over 90% of eligible local workers reaching 62 and those aged 63 to 67 who wish to continue working are offered re-employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Today, well over 90% of the eligible private sector local workers reaching the age of 62 who wish to continue working are offered re-employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Even for those who are 63 to 67 years old, more than 90% of them are offered re-employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Of those who were re-employed in the same job, the vast majority continue to enjoy the same wages during re-employment.
